key_insight: FRIEND uses federated learning to jointly optimize multi‑RIS configurations and intelligent eavesdropper detection across distributed B5G cell‑free mmWave nodes, improving secrecy and detection without centralizing raw data.
problem_solved: Securing distributed CF mmWave B5G/IIoT networks with multiple RIS elements against passive and active eavesdroppers while avoiding centralized data collection and scaling to many edge nodes; conventional centralized or isolated approaches struggle with privacy, latency, and coordination.
method: Design a federated learning pipeline (FRIEND) where edge nodes (APs/RIS controllers/UEs) locally train detection and configuration models and share model updates for privacy‑preserving aggregation.

Joint optimization loop that alternates between learned eavesdropper detection and multi‑RIS configuration (beamforming/profile selection) to maximize secrecy metrics and detection accuracy under realistic mmWave/CF channels.

Lightweight communication and aggregation strategies tailored for IIoT/B5G constraints, plus performance evaluation via simulations comparing secrecy rate and detection error against baseline centralized and non‑cooperative schemes.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, privacy‑aware way to apply federated ML to physical‑layer security and multi‑agent control in next‑generation wireless systems, giving AI/ML practitioners a blueprint for distributed model design and evaluation in edge wireless environments.
visual_elements: Network architecture diagram: cell‑free mmWave layout with multiple RIS panels, APs, UEs, an eavesdropper icon, and a federated aggregator node.
Training flowchart: local data → local model update → secure aggregation → updated RIS configuration → improved detection (looped).
Performance charts: secrecy rate vs. training rounds and detection accuracy vs. number of participating edge nodes (comparison to centralized/baseline).
Icon set: RIS panel, shield/lock for security, magnifying glass for detection, and cloud/server for federated aggregation.
paper_title: FRIEND: Federated Learning for Joint Optimization of multi-RIS Configuration and Eavesdropper Intelligent Detection in B5G Networks
paper_authors: Maria Lamprini A. Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Anastasios K. Papazafeiropoulos, Maria A. Seimeni, Dimitra I. Kaklamani
